questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Social Psychology: Diffusion of Responsibility
questions.learningObjective: Identify when responsibility diffuses across a group.
questions.stem: A developer notices a failing build but assumes a teammate will fix it; what concept explains this inaction?

options.text: The build failure is too minor to matter
options.misconception: minimizes the problem to avoid action

options.text: The developer feels personally responsible and will act immediately
The developer lacks the skill to repair the build
Responsibility is shared so each person waits for others to act

questions.explanation: Diffusion of responsibility occurs when presence of others reduces felt obligation. The tempting skill-gap idea fails because the barrier is social, not technical.
questions.hint: More people present lowers personal obligation.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Social Psychology: Pluralistic Ignorance
questions.learningObjective: Explain pluralistic ignorance in a group setting.
questions.stem: Everyone in a standup stays silent about a risky deadline, though each privately doubts it; explain the shared illusion.

answer.exemplar: Each member privately doubts the deadline but assumes others accept it, so no one speaks; the group mistakes silence for agreement, producing pluralistic ignorance.

questions.explanation: Pluralistic ignorance is when individuals privately reject a norm but assume others accept it. Silence is misread as consensus, so the risky deadline stands.

questions.stem: Randomly assigned labels with no shared history still produce favoritism; explain the minimal group effect.

answer.exemplar: Arbitrary categorization triggers in-group favoritism as people seek positive distinctiveness, even without real group ties or history.

questions.explanation: Minimal groups show labels alone suffice. Positive distinctiveness drives the bias. The exemplar grounds the answer in social Psychology: Group Categories With No History rather than restating the question.

questions.topic: Social Psychology: Diffusion of Responsibility
questions.stem: Twelve on-call engineers receive the same incident alert and none responds for fifteen minutes; explain using diffusion.

answer.exemplar: With twelve recipients, each assumes another will respond, so personal obligation drops and the incident sits unclaimed until ownership is assigned.

questions.explanation: Diffusion scales with recipient count. Assigning a single responder reverses the delay. The exemplar grounds the answer in social Psychology: Diffusion of Responsibility rather than restating the question.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Social Psychology: Pluralistic Ignorance
questions.learningObjective: Spot pluralistic ignorance in a standup.

stimulus.body: In a standup, every member nods at a risky deadline, yet private messages reveal each doubted it. No one wanted to be first to object, so silence looked like agreement and the deadline stood.

questions.stem: One source note on social Psychology: Pluralistic Ignorance notes: "Pluralistic ignorance mistaken for consensus" Taking that statement as given, while reviewing the material, what concept does the nodding illustrate?

options.text: Pluralistic ignorance mistaken for consensus
True group agreement on the deadline
options.misconception: confuses public nods with private belief

options.text: Obedience to a manager's deadline
Social loafing on effort

questions.explanation: Private doubt with public assent is pluralistic ignorance. True agreement would require private acceptance too.
